title: Get a second read of your own MRI scan files
summary: Antoine Finkelstein had Claude Code analyze his shoulder MRI files; it argued, with moderate-to-high confidence, for no tear where the radiologist reported one, and radiologists pushed back.
agent_role: Claude Code processed 266MB of DICOM files, ran analysis scripts and arbitrated between readings; the patient chose what to ask and how far to trust it, with no clinical validation.
outcome: Agent concluded with "moderate-to-high confidence" that the evidence favored no discrete tear, contradicting the Grade III partial-thickness tear reported; radiologists on Hacker News pushed back
what_they_did: Developer Antoine Finkelstein gave Claude Code the 266MB of raw scan files from his own shoulder MRI. He had it write and run its own analysis programs. Then it compared its reading with the radiologist's report. He chose what to ask and how far to trust the answer. No doctor checked the results.
how_it_went: The agent concluded with "moderate-to-high confidence" that the evidence pointed to no clear tear. The radiologist had reported a Grade III partial-thickness tear.
worth_knowing: Radiologists on Hacker News pushed back on the agent's reading. Treat an answer like this as a question to bring to a doctor, not a diagnosis.
prompt: I have the DICOM files from my [body part] MRI in [folder path] and the radiologist's report in [report file]. Inventory the files and explain which series and views are present. Write and run scripts to view and analyze the images relevant to the report's findings. Then compare your observations with each finding in the report. For each one, say whether you agree, what evidence you see, and how confident you are. Clearly list the limits of this analysis. This is not a diagnosis. Give me a list of questions to ask my doctor.

curation.rationale: Reviewed: details (266MB of DICOM files, the Grade III partial-tear report, the model's 'moderate-to-high confidence' arbitration, the Hacker News debate) are corroborated by several independent write-ups.
